name: Bugatti Chiron Pur Sport
description: Quad-turbo 8.0-litre W16 tuned for agility: shorter gearing, a fixed rear wing and lighter wheels make it the most driver-focused Chiron.

name: Koenigsegg Jesko Attack
description: Twin-turbo 5.0-litre V8 and Koenigsegg's nine-speed Light Speed Transmission, with a huge rear wing built for track downforce.

name: Pagani Huayra Roadster BC
description: Hand-built in San Cesario sul Panaro around a twin-turbo Mercedes-AMG V12, with a removable roof and active aero flaps.

name: Lamborghini Revuelto
description: Lamborghini's first V12 plug-in hybrid: a naturally aspirated 6.5-litre V12 plus three electric motors and all-wheel drive.

name: Aston Martin Valkyrie
description: Designed with Adrian Newey around a Cosworth 6.5-litre V12 that revs past 11,000 rpm, with Formula 1-style ground-effect aero.

name: McLaren Senna
description: Named after Ayrton Senna. A track-focused carbon car with a 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8, active aero and glass door panels.

name: Ferrari SF90 Stradale
description: Ferrari's plug-in hybrid flagship: twin-turbo V8 plus three electric motors, all-wheel drive and a short electric-only range.

name: Porsche 911 GT3 RS (992)
description: A 4.0-litre naturally aspirated flat-six that revs to 9,000 rpm, with a swan-neck rear wing and adjustable DRS.

name: McLaren 765LT
description: The Longtail version of the 720S: lighter, more power from the 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8, and a longer active rear wing.

name: Ferrari 296 GTB
description: A twin-turbo V6 plug-in hybrid with a compact, classic Berlinetta shape and a short electric-only mode for the city.

name: Lamborghini Huracán STO
description: Super Trofeo Omologata: a road-legal racer with a 5.2-litre V10, rear-wheel drive and a one-piece carbon bonnet.

name: Maserati MC20
description: Maserati's mid-engined comeback: the in-house Nettuno twin-turbo V6, butterfly doors and a carbon-fibre tub.

name: Rolls-Royce Spectre
description: Rolls-Royce's first electric car: a two-door, four-seat coupé with coach doors and a Starlight headliner.

name: Bentley Continental GT Speed
description: A twin-turbo W12 grand tourer with all-wheel drive and a hand-finished cabin, built in Crewe.

name: Rolls-Royce Phantom
description: The flagship limousine: a 6.75-litre twin-turbo V12, rear coach doors and an art gallery panel across the dashboard.

name: Bentley Flying Spur
description: A four-door Bentley with a chauffeur-friendly rear cabin, rotating dashboard display and a pop-up Flying B mascot.

name: Aston Martin DB12
description: Aston Martin's "super tourer": a twin-turbo V8 and a fully redesigned cabin in a classic long-bonnet DB shape.

name: Mercedes-Maybach S-Class
description: The longest-wheelbase S-Class, with reclining executive rear seats, a chrome pinstripe grille and optional two-tone paint.

name: Lamborghini Urus Performante
description: A lighter, lower Urus with a twin-turbo V8, a carbon bonnet and a Rally driving mode for loose surfaces.

name: Ferrari Purosangue
description: Ferrari's first four-door: a naturally aspirated V12, rear-hinged rear doors and four individual seats.

name: Aston Martin DBX707
description: The most powerful DBX: a twin-turbo V8 with a wet-clutch nine-speed gearbox and big carbon-ceramic brakes.

name: Rolls-Royce Cullinan
description: Rolls-Royce's all-terrain car: a V12, air suspension and a tailgate with pop-out viewing seats.

name: Bentley Bentayga
description: A twin-turbo V8 luxury SUV with a hand-finished cabin and a smooth air-sprung ride.

name: Mercedes-AMG G 63
description: The boxy icon with a hand-built twin-turbo V8, three locking differentials and side-exit exhausts.

name: Rimac Nevera
description: A Croatian electric hypercar with four motors, torque vectoring on every wheel and launch control that redefines quick.

name: Porsche Taycan Turbo GT
description: The fastest Taycan: dual motors, launch-control overboost and an 800-volt architecture for very fast charging.

name: Tesla Model S
description: The car that made long-range electric saloons mainstream: dual-motor all-wheel drive, a big central touchscreen and Supercharger access.

name: Lucid Air
description: A long-range electric luxury saloon with a glass canopy roof and a spacious, limousine-like rear seat.

name: Audi RS e-tron GT
description: A low, wide electric grand tourer that shares its 800-volt platform with the Taycan.

name: BMW i7
description: BMW's electric 7 Series, with a fold-down 31-inch theatre screen for rear passengers.

name: Nissan GT-R
description: The "Godzilla" R35: hand-assembled twin-turbo V6, all-wheel drive and a dual-clutch gearbox.

name: Chevrolet Corvette Stingray
description: The first mid-engined Corvette: a 6.2-litre V8 behind the seats and a removable roof panel.

name: Toyota GR Supra
description: A compact front-engined coupé with a turbo straight-six, offered with a six-speed manual.

name: BMW M4 Competition
description: A twin-turbo straight-six coupé with the bold vertical kidney grille and optional all-wheel drive.

name: Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 RS
description: A mid-engined Cayman with the 4.0-litre flat-six from the 911 GT3 and intake ducts where the rear quarter windows were.

name: Lotus Emira
description: Lotus's last combustion sports car: light, mid-engined and available with a gated six-speed manual.

name: BMW M5 Competition
description: A twin-turbo V8 executive saloon with switchable all-wheel drive, including a rear-drive mode.

name: Mercedes-AMG E 63 S
description: A hand-built twin-turbo V8 in a comfortable business saloon, with a drift mode for track days.

name: Audi RS 7 Sportback
description: A twin-turbo V8 four-door coupé with a liftback boot, all-wheel drive and wide flared arches.

name: Porsche Panamera
description: A four-door Porsche that drives like a sports car, with four individual seats and an active rear spoiler.

name: Maserati Quattroporte
description: An Italian luxury saloon with a Ferrari-derived V8 soundtrack and a classic long-bonnet profile.

name: Alfa Romeo Giulia Quadrifoglio
description: A rear-drive saloon with a Ferrari-derived twin-turbo V6 and a carbon-fibre bonnet and roof.

name: Volkswagen Golf GTI
description: The original hot hatch: a turbocharged four-cylinder, tartan seats and the red stripe across the grille.

name: Volkswagen Golf R
description: The all-wheel-drive Golf, with a torque-vectoring rear axle and quad exhaust tips.

name: Honda Civic Type R
description: A front-drive record breaker with a six-speed manual, a turbo four and a big rear wing.

name: Toyota GR Yaris
description: A rally-bred three-door with a turbo three-cylinder and adjustable all-wheel drive.

name: Mercedes-AMG A 45 S
description: One of the most powerful four-cylinder production engines, in a compact all-wheel-drive hatch.

name: Audi RS 3 Sportback
description: A turbocharged five-cylinder hatch with a torque splitter for rear-biased handling.
